parameters.excerpt: The hardware platform may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered, as defined by the Memory-Ordering PMAs section in Volume II of this manual.

parameters.excerpt: The optional MISP bit is set by the hardware when the recorded transfer is an instruction whose target or taken/not-taken direction was mispredicted by the branch predictor. MISP is read-only 0 when not implemented.

parameters.excerpt: The `ctrdata` register contains metadata for the recorded transfer. This register must be implemented, though all fields within it are optional. Unimplemented fields are read-only 0.
parameters.mentor_verdict: This is a partly normative rule (register must exist), partly WARL behavior . The spec is doesn't use the term WARL, but its definition is the the field is either RW, or RdOnly0 (thus a parameter)

parameters.excerpt: The `ctrdata` register may optionally include a count of CPU cycles elapsed since the prior CTR record.

parameters.excerpt: An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps, with the supported delegatable bits found by writing one to every bit location, then reading back the value in `medeleg` or `mideleg` to see which bit positions hold a one.

parameters.excerpt: Bit 63 of each `mstateen` CSR may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and the matching supervisor-level `sstateen` CSR is all read-only zeros.
parameters.mentor_verdict: why new ?(seems to have a tag- not in UDB?), per bit conditional parameter (sets mask[x]==0 and value[x]==0; true only if (sstateen_mask=0 &stateen_val==0 & exists[H_esxtension))
parameters.resolved_note: The mentor asked whether this is genuinely new ('seems to have a tag -- not in UDB?'). Answered: it is new. The spec tag does exist ([#norm:mstateen-bit-63_roz], smstateen.adoc:175), but UDB defines only six MSTATEEN_*_TYPE parameters (ENVCFG/IMSIC/AIA/CONTEXT/CSRIND/JVT) and none for bit 63. Tagged in the spec does not mean present in UDB.
